messages.author: 48d1979aaecf14b4
messages.subject: Memory usage
parts:
Hello,
I was wondering if there was an upper limit on the number of reads in total that can be analyzed efficiently with methylKit. For example, previous data sets that I have successfully analyzed have had about 60 million reads per sample group, but a new data set has about 120 million reads. The memory usage is becoming a problem when calling the unite function to find common sites between all samples. Previously memory usage has been only a few gigs of RAM, but with new data sets it maxes out memory (8 gigs) and uses about another 8-16 gigs of swap space and never finishes the function.  Is memory usage quadratic for this function? or is there something else going on? Any insights would be greatly appreciated.
Great program by the way. Have used quite a bit for a few different projects.
Thanks,
Jason

messages.author: 48d1979aaecf14b4
messages.subject: Re: Memory usage
parts: I need to clarify one thing. I guess the number of reads is irrelevant, it is the number of sites be analyzed. In my previous analyses, there have been about 500,000 individual sites in each sample with roughly 450,000 in common. With the new data sets, there are about twice that many, with roughly 1 million sites per sample. Finding the sites in common is where the problem is.

messages.author: ab8277113f65c05e
messages.subject: Re: Memory usage
parts:
Hi Jason,
How many samples you have in total? and are you using "min.per group" argument as well? 

unite() function uses the base merge() function successively I am not sure what can be done to make it more efficient but I know if you use "min.per.group" argument, that part is not implemented efficiently. 

As a general advice, I suggest removing the unused objects from your environment with rm() and do garbage collection with gc(T). 

Best,
Altuna

messages.author: 48d1979aaecf14b4
messages.subject: Re: [methylkit_discussion] Re: Memory usage
parts: Problem is solved. There was an issue in our file set where the genomic location for the negative strand reads were listed as relative position instead of actual genomic position. This resulted in multiple sites with the same genomic location being list. After resolving this issue the unite() function has completed with no problems.
